verdicts.title: 6 Bagatelles, Op. 51
verdicts.note: Exists (violin & piano, 1893-94, dedicated to Juliette Folville, Simrock Berlin 1894, plates 10293-98). Only the title wording is off: IMSLP and Wikipedia use numeral + French 'Bagatelles' ('Six' is not in any source). The six pieces are documented, so the set could be split like Op. 50: 1 Arietta, 2 Petit conte, 3 Melodie, 4 A la mazurka, 5 Chant sans paroles, 6 Rondinetto.

verdicts.title: 7 Miniatures, Op. 39
verdicts.note: (not flagged verify) Original for violin & piano, 1886, Bessel St Petersburg c. 1895 (plates 3332-38). IMSLP page title is 'Miniatures, Op.39' but lists 7 pieces; Wikipedia says 'Six/Seven Miniatures' (Leduc's 1886-87 piano selection had 6). Pieces: Marionettes espagnoles (C), Romanzetta (D), En partant (E-flat), Arabesque (D), Au berceau (G), Feuille d'album (E-flat), Petite marche (D). Numbered title is optional; keeping 'Miniatures, Op. 39' is also acceptable.

verdicts.title: 2 Morceaux, Op. 24
verdicts.note: Exists: IMSLP '2 Morceaux, Op.24', violin with orchestra (or piano), composed 1884, publ. 1885; violin & piano edition Hamburg, D. Rahter, plates 2535-36 (28 pp.). 'Two' is not in the sources - use numeral + French. The two pieces are documented: 1 Alla spagnuola (A minor), 2 Nocturne (A major) - could be split into two entries if wanted. Wikipedia: 'Deux Morceaux, Op. 24 ... violin, with orchestra or piano accompaniment'.

(not flagged verify) Violin & piano, 1879 (Buttner/Rahter, Leipzig, plate 2022), dedicated to Grand Duke Paul Alexandrovich; 6 pieces: Au crepuscule, Valse, Scherzino, Romance, Serenade, Finale. Wikipedia: 'Petite suite, Op. 14 (1879, publ. 1890), piano and violin'.

(not flagged verify) 'Tarantella' for violin & piano in C minor, composed 1893, Simrock Berlin 1894 (plate 10090); no opus number. Wikipedia lists 'Tarantelle for violin and piano (1893)'. Not to be confused with Tarantella in G minor, Op. 12 (orchestra).

(not flagged verify) IMSLP: 'Valse melancolique' in C minor for violin (or 'concertino') and piano, dedicated to Mme B. Doukhovskoy, P. Jurgenson Moscow 1911 (plate 35584); no opus number. Single IMSLP source only (not in Wikipedia's list); Japanese anthology page also confirms the title/year.

(not flagged verify) Violin Sonata in D major, Op. 84, 3 movements (Allegro; Andante non troppo in B minor; Allegro), dedicated to Boris Michalowsky, composed c. 1860-70 (?), first published by Jurgenson, Moscow 1911 (plate 35095). Wikipedia: 'Op. 84 Sonata, c. 1860-1870; publ. 1911'. Early-period work published late; the 'Romantic sonata' description is fair.

gaps.title: 12 Miniatures, Op. 20
gaps.scoring: violin and piano (the composer's own arrangement of his 12 Miniatures for piano, 1882)
gaps.edition: V. Bessel & Co., St Petersburg 1885 (plates 1822-33), violin & piano; Berceuse (No. 8) also published separately for violin & piano by J. Oertel, Berlin; Berceuse also arr. Carse (Muzgiz 1963)
gaps.note: Pieces: 1 Expansion naive, 2 Aveu timide, 3 Petite valse, 4 A la Schumann, 5 Cantabile, 6 Souvenir douloureux, 7 Mosaique, 8 Berceuse, 9 Canzonetta, 10 Petite marche, 11 Mazurka, 12 Scherzo rustique (all documented, so could be split like Op. 50; Nos. 5 and 8 are the best known). Second source: Wikipedia's Cui work list gives 'Op. 20 Twelve Miniatures (1882), violin and piano (also for piano solo)'. Recording evidence not checked; level 3 matches Op. 39/Op. 50.
